column1: # Known gaps: our open bugs, each one with a todo behind it.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a gap of ours -- a call plain Metal answers and we refuse, or a field that
# differs with nothing announced to justify it -- which, by the owner's standing rule that what
# Metal allows we must allow, is a bug of ours, written down so the one case that holds it visible
# does not make every run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. An accepted difference
# lives in `docs/API.md` section 10 and is justified; a degradation lives in the degrade catalogue
# and is announced. This file is neither. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# It is an EXPECTATION, NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and `conformance replay` holds it to that in both
# directions, per venue:
#   - a refusal or a divergence that is not listed here fails the run: a new gap appeared;
#   - a row listed here that the run no longer holds ALSO fails the run, saying the gap looks
#     fixed and the row must go.
# That second direction is the whole point. Closing a gap forces the ledger edit, so a row cannot
# outlive the bug it stands for and this file cannot rot into a silencer. It also means a row is
# checked by execution rather than by discipline, which is the standard the rest of the suite is
# held to. It has already earned its keep twice in this round: a product fix landed and the replay
# named four stale rows before anyone reasoned about the fix.
# The ledger changes the exit status and nothing else. The report still prints each of these as a
# `Refused` or `Divergent` row, with our answer and Metal's, with Metal's own words where its API
# validation refuses the call too, and counted in the suite's own numbers. Nothing is laundered.
# A row is held only against the cases a run selected and the venues it ran on, so replaying one
# case does not read every other row as fixed, and a run on one venue does not read another
# venue's rows as fixed.
# Tab-separated, SIX fields. Blank lines and lines from `#` are ignored.
#   case        the case's name.
#   venue       `*` for every venue, or words held (without case, as a substring) against the
#               venue's own description: its device name, driver, API version and Metal level.
#               `*` is the STRONGER claim, not the looser one -- the second direction then holds
#               the row on every venue the run selected the case on -- so widening a row's scope
#               makes it harder to satisfy, which is what stops a venue-scoped row from becoming a
#               way to silence a venue. A pattern that matches nothing holds the row nowhere, so
#               its gap reads as unlisted and the run fails: a typo is loud.
#   expects     `refused`, a call plain Metal answered and we did not; or `divergent`, a field that
#               differs with nothing announced to justify it. Nothing else is ever written down:
#               an unrecorded case and a stale recording must fail loudly, and a venue that
#               honestly lacks a feature is not a gap of ours at all.
#   site        the site, as node names from the root, exactly as the report prints it.
#   answer      what the run answers there, exactly as the report prints it after the site, which
#               `conformance replay` also emits as a ready-to-paste row so nobody has to
#               reconstruct it. For a refusal that is our typed error. For a divergence it is how
#               much moved: how many of the site's leaves differ and the largest difference where
#               the values are numbers. NOT the first mismatch -- a bound read off the first
#               mismatch is not a bound (four rotated-target rows differ by one code at their
#               first mismatch and reach two well past it), and a walk position is a property of
#               the data rather than of the bug, so it would rename the row whenever an earlier
#               leaf moved. The report prints that position on the line below, where it helps a
#               reader and binds nothing. Part of the row's identity, so a gap that changed into
#               another gap at the same site is a new gap and not this one.
#   waiting on  the open bug, in words: what Metal does, what we do instead, and where the fix
#               belongs. Not matched -- it is what a reader needs -- but a row must carry one.
# A row whose case is not in the tree yet cannot be committed: a test holds every live row to a
# case that exists AND to a site that case's committed recording actually holds, so a row for a
# site the case never produces is impossible rather than silently unheld. Leave such a row here as
# a `#` comment for the stream that owns the case; nothing is waiting today.
# case

column1: mesh-object-draws-partial-threadgroup-6-by-4
column5: Err(Error::Bind("the bind state was refused: Unsupported(Unsupported { feature: MeshShading, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: None })"))
column6: The runtime refuses `drawMeshThreads` where the threads leave a partial object threadgroup, `Unsupported(MeshShading, NotImplemented)` out of the bind state (crates/metal2vulkan/src/bind/graphics.rs, `mesh_draw`'s `threads[i].is_multiple_of(lo[i])` test), while Metal draws it and runs the threads left over. Not a device gap: this M3 Max has mesh shading and draws every other row of the same probe. Measured on it (macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, our probe gaps/mesh/obj, one shape per process): the draw launches ceil(threads/L) object threadgroups, `threads_per_grid` is the threads asked for, and the last threadgroup on an axis runs with the threads left over as a non-uniform threadgroup exactly as `dispatchThreads:` does for compute - `threads_per_threadgroup` is min(L, threads - group*L) per axis (6 of 64 reports 6), `thread_position_in_threadgroup` and `thread_index_in_threadgroup` run over that reduced size, `simdgroups_per_threadgroup` is ceil of it over 32, and a threadgroup barrier synchronizes the threads left over alone. The cause is that Vulkan has no partial workgroup: the exact form is the one compute already uses, a region per edge dispatched at its own local size, which for a draw means several draws of several pipeline specializations and, on a grid with more than one whole threadgroup on a higher axis, a primitive order that is not Metal's; the alternative is one draw of ceil groups with the object entry reading its reduced size from its `DispatchRegion` record (`MultiRegion` 1 already carries the grid and L, and already reports ceil threadgroups and the asked-for threads), deriving the thread position and index from `lin` over that size and returning before the body past it, which is exact for everything but a threadgroup barrier and so needs a pipeline variant whose compile refuses an object function that synchronizes. Neither is built. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

column1: discard-quad-sum-placement
column6: Metal counts the quads the discard drops whole in a simdgroup sum that sits ahead of the discard for a measured reason -- the discard's condition reads the sum (`counted_dependent`), or a device store (`counted_store`) or an atomic (`counted_atomic`) lies between them -- so each kept texel's first channel, `before > after`, is 1. On llvmpipe all four texels of the kept quad read 0, uniformly and each by exactly one code: our run's sum saw the same lane count before and after the discard. MoltenVK on this M3 Max answers Metal's 1 exactly, with no notice, so this is one venue's difference and not the module's rule being wrong (verified: a whole-set replay on each venue, 2026-10-23). The cause is NOT established, and the case as written cannot establish it: the four numbers it records per texel are identical under both candidates -- the device's fragment simdgroup holding only the kept quad, so the dropped quads were never in it (the target is 8 by 4, exactly one 32-lane simdgroup if the device packs it that way), and the device's compiler moving the reduction past the discard although `canon/discard_sink.rs` placed it ahead on purpose. Both give before == after and so (0, 0, 0, 0), on every texel alike, which is why the uniformity across the quad separates nothing either. The next step is the case's: record the simdgroup's own size and the raw `before` and `after` beside the four derived numbers, which separates the two at no cost, then fix whichever it is -- a device whose reduction does not see the dropped lanes needs the active set computed in the module rather than taken from the device's implicit one (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/simd/group.rs with crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/discard_sink.rs), and a device whose fragment simdgroup is smaller than Metal's is a different answer again. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list, handed to whoever takes the discard-hoist family.

column1: sparse-tails-wide-and-short
column6: Metal's `tailSizeInBytes` exceeds our sparse model's on extreme aspect ratios: a 2D texture whose shorter axis is a handful of texels while the longer is a thousand or more. Each row's own two numbers are in its answer field. Measured, and sharper than it was: EVERY one of the 13 differences is a whole multiple of the 16384-byte page -- eleven of them one page, two of them (RGBA32Float, levels-4, 1000x3 and 3x1000) two pages -- and the answers are symmetric in the axes, so 1000x3 and 3x1000 give identical numbers for every format. The page count differs per format, and the rule that produces it is still unidentified; what is now established is that our model is short by whole pages rather than by a rounding, which rules out an alignment or ceiling error inside a page. The rows are scoped to every venue because the answer is CPU arithmetic over a descriptor in `crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture/heap_tiled.rs`, the same model on every device at one Metal level: verified identical, site for site and number for number, on MoltenVK on this M3 Max and on llvmpipe in the Linux container (2026-10-23), which is why `*` and not a venue. We believe Metal's answer and our model must both be re-derived before a fix: the model was fitted to ordinary shapes and these are outside what it was fitted to. No tolerance is right here -- the number is a byte count Metal states exactly, and a consumer sizing a heap from it would under-allocate. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list for the sparse stream.

column1: argb8-targets-destination-alpha
column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: Some(RenderPipeline at Color(0)), symbol: None }"))
column6: Plain Metal on this M3 Max makes and runs a render pipeline whose ARGB8Unorm colour attachment blends with DestinationAlpha and OneMinusDestinationAlpha in the COLOUR factors, and stores every texel as the RGBA8Unorm leg's bytes rotated (recorded here over 3 runs, 8,192 texels, zero mismatches; Metal's own API validation let it run). The runtime refuses the pipeline Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented) at colour attachment 0, so the refusal is of something plain Metal does. The cause is structural rather than a policy: the runtime holds ARGB8Unorm in an R8G8B8A8_UNORM image of the rotated bytes, so the image's alpha channel carries Metal's BLUE and a colour factor that must read Metal's destination alpha would have to read the image's red. Vulkan has no such blend factor. The alpha-factor direction is already solved -- a second pipeline output of copies of Metal's source alpha (pipeline::rotated_blend) -- but that trick does not reach a DESTINATION channel, which only the framebuffer holds. The exact forms are a pass that keeps the rotated image's channels in Metal's order behind a swizzled view, or reading the destination in the fragment where the device offers programmable blending. Neither is built. Fix belongs in metal2vulkan's pipeline (rotated_blend) and the runtime's ARGB8Unorm image layout. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

column1: shared-event-handle-round-trip
column6: A Metal SHARED event answers NIL for `device`, and the runtime answers the device it was made on. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, a one-off Objective-C probe outside the suite): `[[dev newEvent] device]` answers the device (registryID 4294968395), while `[[dev newSharedEvent] device]` and the event reopened from its `newSharedEventHandle` both answer nil. So `MTLEvent`'s `device` is one answer for a plain event and another for a shared one, and `metal2vulkan-runtime`'s `SharedEvent::device` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/event.rs, the `device` getter the shared event shares with `Event`) gives the device in both. The case's site is the portable form of the getter -- whether the device is the one the case's other objects were made on -- so Metal's nil reads as false and ours as true. Not a device gap: the probe and the case ran on the same chip, and the plain event's getter agrees on both sides. The fix belongs in the runtime's event module, as a shared event answering no device, and it is a one-line change behind a decision the owner has not been asked for: a consumer that reads a shared event's device today gets an answer, and giving it nil is a change to the published API's behaviour. Nothing else of the pair differs -- the label, the handle's label, the reopened label, every value and both waits compare exactly -- so this row is the whole of the difference.

column1: compute-descriptor-reset
column6: Metal's `MTLComputePipelineDescriptor.reset` is PARTIAL. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434), from `compute-descriptor-reset`'s own committed recording over three runs: the reset restores the label to nil, every `buffers[i].mutability` to `MTLMutabilityDefault`, `supportIndirectCommandBuffers` and `supportAddingBinaryFunctions` to false and `maxCallStackDepth` to 1, and leaves its three thread-shape properties exactly as the program set them -- `threadGroupSizeIsMultipleOfThreadExecutionWidth` true, `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` 96, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` 8 by 6 by 2. The runtime has no descriptor object, so the coverage map's counterpart for `reset` is `ComputePipelineDescriptor::new` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/descriptor.rs), a fresh value that resets all nine, and our side answers 0, 0 and false where Metal answers what was set. Nothing is announced for it, so by the standing rule it is a gap of ours. It is also very likely an Apple defect rather than a contract: in the same round `MTLTileRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores the analogous `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` and `threadgroupSizeMatchesTileSize` correctly (`tile-descriptor-reset` is exact) and `MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores every field it has (`mesh-descriptor-reset` is exact), so only the compute descriptor keeps anything. The fix is a choice between two forms and neither may be guessed at: a `ComputePipelineDescriptor::reset` that mirrors Metal's three kept fields, or an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10 saying a reset compute descriptor keeps its thread shape on Metal and not here. Mirroring an Apple bug in a published crate's API is the owner's call, so this is on the orchestrator's todo list rather than fixed here. Not a device gap: no venue is involved -- the difference is Metal's recorded answer against a plain Rust struct, so the row is every venue's.

column1: resource-aliasing
column6: `Texture::resource_options` does not carry the hazard tracking mode it resolved. Metal never reports `MTLHazardTrackingModeDefault` from a resource: it resolves the descriptor's `Default` and reports the result, which for a texture made outside a heap is `Tracked` -- so its `resourceOptions` holds 0x200 beside the storage field (0x200 shared, 0x220 private, measured on this M3 Max under Metal 27.0.1). The runtime resolves it too, and correctly: `Texture::hazard_tracking_mode` answers `Tracked` here and agrees with Metal at every site of these cases, because it reads `Identity::new(mode, in_heap)`'s already-resolved flag (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/resource.rs:57). What it does NOT do is put that resolved field back into the option word: `Texture::resource_options` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture.rs:4759) hands back the descriptor's options as asked for, so the hazard field stays 0. `Buffer::resource_options` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/buffer.rs:3355), `Heap::resource_options` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/heap.rs:842) and `IndirectCommandBuffer::resource_options` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/indirect_command_buffer.rs:3111) each document and do the resolution, and each agrees with Metal in these same cases -- a heap's answers are exact at every site of `heap-own-getters`, including an `Untracked` resolved from `Default` -- so the texture is the one resource of the four that does not. The fix is to report the resolved field: give `ResourceOptions` a `with_hazard_tracking_mode` beside its own shifts (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/values.rs:120, which is where the bit positions live and the only place they should be written) and have `Texture::resource_options` apply `self.hazard_tracking_mode()` through it, keeping `PRIVATE_BIT`. It is deliberately NOT done in this change: `Texture::resource_options` is read inside the runtime as well as by a consumer (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/buffer_texture.rs:1075 reads a tracked flag off an option word), so moving it is a behaviour change in a published crate and needs its own evidence, which this stream has not taken. The three mode getters are each read through their own getter on both sides for exactly this reason, so this row is the option word alone and not the mode. Scoped to this venue because that is where it was measured; the answer is the runtime's own record and so is expected to be every venue's, which is unaudited. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list, for whoever takes the runtime's resource surface.

column1: sparse-mapping-a-level-past-the-textures
column5: Err(Error::Invalid("invalid use of update_texture_mappings: Sparse(Level { level: 9, levels: 9 })"))
column6: The runtime refuses a direct mapping update of a mip level past the texture's own levels, where plain Metal takes the call and maps nothing. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this case's own committed recording over three runs: `updateTextureMapping:mode:region:mipLevel:slice:` of level 9 of a nine-level 256x256 R32Float sparse texture answers, the command buffer completes, and the sparse heap's `usedSize` is 0 before and 0 after -- Metal mapped nothing and refused nothing. Ours answers Invalid(Sparse(Level)) at crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/sparse/mapping.rs:500, in `UnitGrid::checked_region`, whose own doc says the refusal is there because Metal's VALIDATION stops it; the suite's second oracle confirms that half -- Metal's API validation layer prints `mipLevel(9) must be <= [texture firstMipmapInTail](3)` -- so the two oracles disagree and the runtime follows the stricter one. It also disagrees with ITSELF: `UnitGrid::clipped_region` (mapping.rs:467), which the indirect selector uses, returns no units for exactly this input and so matches plain Metal, and `update_texture_mapping_indirect`'s doc says so outright. By the owner's standing rule that what Metal allows we must allow, the direct path is the one that is wrong. The fix is one of two forms and neither may be guessed at: make `checked_region` clip a level or slice past the texture's as `clipped_region` does and map nothing, which makes the direct and indirect paths one behaviour and follows plain Metal; or keep the refusal and record an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10 saying the runtime follows Metal's validation here. The first changes a published crate's documented refusal surface and the runtime's own tests assert the refusal, so it is the owner's call rather than this packet's. The same question stands for `SparseProblem::Slice` (mapping.rs:505) and `SparseProblem::Region` (mapping.rs:520), which no case covers yet. Not a device gap: no venue is involved -- the refusal is in the encoder, before any Vulkan call -- so the row is every venue's.

column1: function-bindings-visible-function-table
column6: Metal compiles a kernel that takes a `visible_function_table` argument and links no visible function, and reflects it: the binding is listed as `MTLBindingTypeVisibleFunctionTable` at buffer 1 (measured on this M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal and under its API validation, which let the case run). The runtime refuses the creation instead: devirtualization (crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/devirt.rs, the `NeedsInput(MissingInput::VisibleFunctionTable)` at the surviving table call) requires the stage to link at least one function of the call's type, on the reasoning that otherwise no entry can hold a callee. Metal's own answer is that such a table is simply null or empty at run time and the shader's `is_null_visible_function_table` and `size()` guards take that path -- which is exactly what `visible_table_caller.metal` does. The fix belongs in devirtualization: where nothing is linked, lower the call site to the null-table behaviour the runtime already documents for an unbound index (a zero-filled neutral, size 0) rather than refusing the compile, so a kernel that only ever reads an empty table still makes a pipeline state. The passing shape of this same case is a second one with linked functions, which needs an `MTLLinkedFunctions` spec in the suite's vocabulary and does not exist yet.

column1: function-bindings-data-types-tables
column6: The same gap as the `function-bindings-visible-function-table` row above, reached through an argument buffer instead of a buffer slot, which is why it is a second row and not that one: the refusal names a different input (`buffer: None`, the table having no slot of its own) and a gap's identity here is its case, its site and its answer. Metal compiles `reflection/tables_in_arguments`' `reflection_tables_in_arguments` -- whose argument buffer holds one `visible_function_table<uint(uint)>` at id 0, an inline `uint` at id 1 and an `array<visible_function_table<uint(uint)>, 2>` at id 2 -- with no `MTLLinkedFunctions` at all, and reflects the whole tree: the member and the array elements are `MTLDataTypeVisibleFunctionTable`, and the array carries the stride and argumentIndexStride Metal derived (measured on this M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal; its API validation let the case run). The runtime refuses the creation in devirtualization (crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/devirt.rs:1848, the `NeedsInput(MissingInput::VisibleFunctionTable)` raised where a surviving table call has no function of its type to switch over), although the library itself defines a matching `[[visible]] uint reflection_table_step(uint)`: the function is exported rather than address-taken, so nothing reaches the call site's word and the arm list comes out empty. The fix is the one the earlier row names -- where nothing is linked, lower the call to the null-table behaviour the runtime already documents for an unbound index rather than refusing the compile -- and it closes both rows together, which is the point of keeping them side by side. This row exists because the argument-buffer reach was unmeasured before this case: the earlier row's evidence is a table in a buffer slot, and a claim is only as broad as its evidence. Every other site of this case is unreached while the creation refuses, so the data types its argument buffer states are recorded from Metal and compared against nothing of ours until the fix lands. Not a device gap: the refusal is in translation, before any Vulkan call, so the row is every venue's. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list, with the row above.
